profile.reading:
This OSM record, "Centersquare Ashburn IAD4 Data Center," is a separately mapped point referencing the same IAD4 campus already tracked in this dataset under two distinct street-addressed records, IAD4-A at 21561 Beaumeade Circle and IAD4-B at 21571 Beaumeade Circle, Ashburn, Virginia 20147; this record's own OSM tags carry no independent street address, only a reference code "IAD4" and a link to Csquare's Northern Virginia page's Ashburn IAD4 anchor. Given that Csquare's own materials, both its public spec sheet and its SEC Form S-1 property table, describe only one IAD4 campus rather than a third distinct Ashburn facility, this record is treated as a likely duplicate or campus-level re-listing of the same IAD4-A/IAD4-B site rather than a genuinely separate ninth Northern Virginia building, consistent with this dataset's practice of flagging apparent duplicates rather than inventing an unconfirmed tenth building. Csquare (formerly branded Centersquare, launched April 2024 by Brookfield Infrastructure to combine Cyxtera, acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy for $775 million in a deal completed January 2024, and Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business under Brookfield since 2019) went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share. Csquare's public spec sheet states a campus-wide 57,927 square feet of raised floor, 35.8 megawatts of utility power, 16.8 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 20 megawatts of generator capacity across the whole IAD4 campus.

Csquare's Northern Virginia footprint, spread across IAD1, IAD2, IAD3, and IAD4 campuses in Sterling, Dulles, and Ashburn, sits within Loudoun County's Data Center Alley, the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, alongside dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators. Csquare's SEC S-1 discloses 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity across its full 64-facility, 21-market portfolio as of March 31, 2026, of which Northern Virginia represents a substantial share given the four separate campuses tracked in this dataset.

reading.body:
Centersquare Ashburn IAD4 is a 238.7 MW campus in Loudoun County, Virginia, making it the 24th largest published data center by power capacity in a state that lists 1,375 MW across 23 facilities with public specifications. The campus holds security certifications for SOC compliance, PCI payment processing, and standards-based information security frameworks. Note that the operator's current market page describes this Ashburn location as a single 35.8 MW facility, while this registry carries three clustered rows in the same area; the 238.7 MW figure may represent either multiple buildings on one campus or a data fragmentation issue requiring clarification by future research.

At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the 238.7 MW campus would accommodate roughly 6,000 racks of compute, though this assumes all utility power reaches the IT floor and ignores cooling, networking, and other overhead. The 269,000 square feet of technical space would then yield roughly 0.023 MW per square foot, consistent with dense hyperscale hosting but below the 0.04+ MW per square foot of cutting-edge AI-focused campuses. These ratios suggest the facility was designed for conventional enterprise and cloud tenants rather than optimized for the highest-density AI training loads.

Virginia ranks among the top states for published data center capacity and hosts significant cloud and enterprise operations in Loudoun County, though recent AI infrastructure expansion has concentrated new capacity in other regions. This campus, if it represents a single operational unit rather than multiple facilities, ranks below the largest published Virginia campuses and falls in the middle range of the state's disclosed capacity. Its certifications and scale indicate it serves established workloads, not the nascent supply-constrained edge of AI acceleration.
